about: Adapter between this proof and the operations other fronts are adding. `op`/`args` of `export` are the CONTRACT TARGET (docs/migration/next-delivery-ten-agents.md, frozen contract 3: scene.export {scene,preset,destination,from,frames,wait?}); every other field is an ADDITIVE proposal and is marked `proposed`. `$name` is replaced by the phase's value, a null value drops the key. A phase sends the real request; `unknown_operation` makes that phase BLOCKED (exit 3), never PASS. No editor rule lives in this file or in the harness: the coordinator edits names after R1 lands, no phase code changes.

export.needs: scene.export {scene, preset, destination, from, frames, wait?} through the shared parser (core ops::parse_op), a snapshot of the scene taken at the request, frames [from, from+frames), the plan and approved resources of scene.render, a job with progress/cancel (job.get/job.cancel), staging + publish by rename

result.about: Paths into the body answered by a successful export (wait=true) or into `job.get`.result. Every field is OPTIONAL: when present it is compared with what ffprobe measured in the file (a report that lies fails); when absent it is listed as `unreported` in the evidence, never assumed.
result.status: confirmed against R1's delivered report (docs/migration/next-r1-report.md): destination, frames, fps, duration_seconds, output, audio, warnings, verification and frame_hashes/metrics and `resources` ([{asset, sha256, revision, bytes}], checked against the bundle's own contentHash/revisionId) are answered. `fps` is an object {num,den,fps} (Rate::to_json): compared as the exact fraction num/den, `fps` (a float) is ignored.

async.about: wait=false (or the interactive window host) answers {job, state:'queued', info}; the result then comes from job.get.result when job.state is `succeeded`
async.status: same shape as export.start: wait=false answers {job, state, ...}; result from job.get.result (exercised by export_cancel and export_snapshot)

error_codes.about: Codes this proof accepts for refusals. A refusal must be typed (non-empty `code`); these only name the ones the contract is expected to use.

ui.about: Prepared, not wired: the coordinator integrates the export control (frozen contract 4; real id `flow.export_scene`, R1 dialog). The phase looks for these ids in the live tree of an isolated editor instance. While none exists it is BLOCKED; once one exists it STAYS BLOCKED until a verified semantic flow (invoke/set only, then export and verify like socket_export) is written against the integrated build: finding a node is never a PASS.
